anti_rescue: After the first primary begins, do not change task families, candidate feature space, executable semantics, four-evaluation budget, 80% acceptance ratio, inherited policy, controls, 8-point thresholds, or economics. Freeze pass, tie, loss, or execution failure. Any redesign gets a new experiment ID.
claim_boundary: A pass establishes only executable transfer of the exact frozen RIL-RANK-001 ordering signal in this controlled microtask protocol.

A pass does not establish Level 4 recursive improvement, recursive self-improvement, live-agent productivity advantage, repeatability, production value, universal task-family transfer, or hostile-process isolation.

The history-shuffled control tests whether correct binding of the inherited history-derived policy still contributes beyond a policy trained on the same outcome multiset with broken feature/outcome binding.
The receiver-defined microtasks are executable but constructed; they are not a claim about external repositories.
No hard pruning occurs. Ranking changes evaluation order only.

If this experiment does not transfer, do not fund a larger live recursive campaign around this ranker without a new mechanism. If it transfers, the next boundary is a matched live-agent test with equal history access and only the inherited search policy differing.

economics.rule: Report the inherited calibration cost separately from downstream evaluation savings. No new calibration cost is added here. A positive predictive transfer can remain uneconomic at this scale.

question: Does the exact ranking policy frozen by RIL-RANK-001 transfer from its synthetic calibration to fresh receiver-executed microtasks, finding acceptable improvements within the same fixed evaluation budget more often and with fewer downstream evaluations?

task_design.outcome_source: receiver executes candidate implementation against correctness oracle and deterministic operation-count objective; not the RIL-RANK-001 synthetic gain function
